I had an important meeting scheduled for nine o'clock on Monday morning.
I planned everything carefully the night before.
I even chose my clothes and packed my bag early.
On Monday, I woke up on time and felt completely ready.
I ate a quick breakfast and left home with enough time to spare.
The morning felt calm and normal at first.
I walked to the bus stop, checking my phone for the schedule.
The bus was supposed to arrive in five minutes.
I waited, but five minutes passed, then ten minutes more.
The bus finally arrived fifteen minutes late, without any explanation.
I got on, feeling a little nervous now about the time.
I checked the time again and did the math quickly in my head.
The bus moved slowly through traffic, much slower than usual that day.
I watched the minutes pass on my phone screen anxiously.
My meeting was starting in ten minutes, and I was still far away.
I got off the bus two stops early and decided to walk fast.
My bag felt heavy, and my shoes were not made for walking quickly.
Still, I kept moving as fast as I could, weaving around slower people on the sidewalk.
I arrived at the office building right at nine o'clock exactly.
I ran to the elevator and pressed the button many times.
It didn't work that way, of course, no matter how many times I pressed it.
I finally reached the meeting room seven minutes late overall.
Everyone was already sitting around the table waiting.
I opened the door quietly, but every head turned toward me anyway, and my face turned a little red.
My manager gave me a small smile and told me to sit down.
I apologized quickly and explained about the bus delay.
Nobody seemed too upset, and the meeting continued normally after that, much to my relief.
After the meeting, a coworker told me the bus is always late on Mondays.
She said she takes an earlier one just to be safe.
I wished someone had told me that sooner, before I ran through half the building.
Now, on Monday mornings, I take the earlier bus, just like she suggested.
I would rather wait twenty extra minutes than run through the office again.
One late morning taught me to always plan for delays, especially on the first day of the week.
